Reporting to the Chief Data Officer, the role turns strategy into reliable platforms, pipelines, APIs and AI/ML infrastructure used by clinical, research and operational teams. This is a hands-on leadership role in NHG’s data and AI transformation. The Director leads engineering delivery, architecture and standards, builds a multi-disciplinary team, and works with CDO, IT, analytics and clinical stakeholders to ensure NHG’s data infrastructure is secure, reliable, interoperable and scalable. The role is accountable for technology delivery and for the clinical, operational and business outcomes enabled by data and AI engineering. Scope and Interfaces Reports to the Chief Data Officer and leads the engineering function within the Data and AI Office. Owns engineering delivery, technical architecture, engineering standards, platform production readiness and engineering assurance for data and AI products, ensuring alignment with NHG Health’s technology partners, MOH requirements, and Singapore’s national data engineering strategy and digital health initiatives. Partners with the CDO to ensure the engineering roadmap is directly tied to measurable clinical, operational, research and population health outcomes, and that engineering investment decisions are communicated in terms of business value to senior stakeholders. Partners with IT, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, infrastructure and procurement teams on hosting, cloud, network, identity, security, resilience and enterprise technology standards. Works with data governance, clinical informatics, responsible AI, privacy and compliance teams to translate policy requirements into technical controls. Collaborates with clinical, operational, research, population health and corporate stakeholders to convert use cases into scalable engineering solutions. Key Responsibilities 1. Lead design of NHG data strategy and its translation into engineering delivery Design and execute NHG’s data and AI strategy into a clear engineering roadmap, delivery plan and prioritised backlog aligned to clinical, operational, research and population health goals. 2. Build and run data and AI platforms Design, build and operate secure, scalable platforms, pipelines, APIs and AI/ML infrastructure that support trusted data use across NHG with DataOps/MLOPs/AIOps capabilities. 3. Ensure reliability and production readiness Set standards for performance, uptime, monitoring, incident response, documentation and continuous improvement of production data and AI service, with day 2 monitoring for AI capabilities. 4. Embed security, privacy and responsible AI Translate governance, data protection, HIM and responsible AI requirements into practical engineering controls, audit evidence and safe operating practices. 5. Lead and grow the engineering team Recruit, develop and lead a multi-disciplinary engineering team with strong technical discipline, delivery accountability, continuous learning and future skill proofing. 6. Manage technology and vendor choices Evaluate tools, platforms, vendors and build-versus-buy options based on scalability, interoperability, security, cost, supportability and alignment with national technology initiatives in collaboration with health tech agencies. 7. Partner across NHG and national initiatives Work with CDO, IT, cybersecurity, governance, analytics, clinical, corporate and national stakeholders to translate needs into practical engineering solutions and communicate progress, risks and value clearly. Overview of Key Results Areas The role will be assessed against key results areas that show how data and AI engineering enables NHG’s clinical, operational, research and population health priorities. Platform delivery: Secure, scalable and reusable data and AI platforms aligned with NHG and national priorities. Production readiness: Priority data products and AI solutions safely moved into monitored, sustainable use. Governance-by-design: Security, privacy, data governance, HIM and responsible AI built into engineering practices. Capability building: Strong engineering team with mature DevOps, DataOps, MLOps and production support practices. Value and impact: Reduced duplication, trusted data products, faster delivery and measurable clinical, operational and research value, and user satisfactions. Key Requirements Essential At least 12 years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, platform engineering or related technology leadership roles. At least 5 years leading multi-disciplinary engineering teams in complex enterprise environments. Strong technical depth in data engineering, cloud infrastructure, API design, integration architecture, modern software engineering and production operations. Proven experience delivering enterprise-grade platforms or digital systems with strong reliability, security, supportability and governance expectations. Experience with DevOps, DataOps, ALOps and or MLOps practices, including CI/CD, automated testing, monitoring, observability and infrastructure-as-code. Demonstrated ability to communicate engineering strategy, technical trade-offs and delivery risks in business and clinical terms to senior non-technical stakeholders. Experience managing engineering cost transparency, total cost of ownership and value-for-money reporting. Ability to communicate technical trade-offs, delivery risks, value and implementation options clearly to clinical, operational, governance and executive stakeholders. Preferred Healthcare, public-sector or other regulated-industry technology experience. Experience with AI/ML platforms, MLOps, LLM-enabled solutions, generative AI or agentic AI in production settings. Familiarity with healthcare interoperability, clinical safety, data governance, data protection and HIM-related requirements. Experience managing vendors, technology partners, build-vs-buy decisions and value-for-money assessments in enterprise settings. Familiarity with Singapore's national technology landscape, including GovTech platforms, MOH digital health initiatives or whole-of-government cloud and data infrastructure. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field; a Master's degree is an advantage. Institution All Job Function All Job ID All Employment Type All Clear Search Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Create Alert × Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Apply now » Director, Business Operations and Go-to-Market Job ID: 9175 Job Function: Administration Institution: National University Health System Job Title: Director, Business Operations and Go-to-Market (BizOps & GTM) Reports to: Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Role Overview We are seeking a high-capacity operator and strategic leader to join our leadership team as the Director of Business Operations & Go-to-Market. Reporting directly to the CEO, this hybrid role integrates company-level business operations, commercial execution, and health-system AI adoption leadership—ensuring that EndeavourX’s products achieve real-world clinical and operational impact across NUHS and external clients. This is a pivotal role for a fast-growing AI spinout. You will: • Drive operational excellence across multiple functions. • Lead cross-functional GTM strategy and execution. • Oversee AI workflow integration, adoption, and benefits realisation with health-system partners. • Act as an organisational force multiplier, building structure, cadence, and accountability as the company scales. The role will suit a strategic thinker with strong stakeholder management, a builder’s mindset, and exceptional ability to execute in a dynamic startup–enterprise hybrid environment. As the company grows, this role offers a pathway toward expanded senior leadership responsibilities. Key Responsibilities 1. Business Operations (BizOps) Strategic & Cross-Functional Operations • Partner with CEO/COO to integrate day-to-day operations across legal, finance, HR, product, clinical, data science, and customer-facing teams. • Establish and lead the BizOps function, including OKR setting, quarterly business reviews, operating rhythms, and cross-functional execution cadences. • Develop and standardise company-wide processes to support internal scaling (hiring, onboarding, budgeting, resource planning), and external scaling (product deployments, customer engagements). Organisational Structure & Leadership • Build operating models to align clinical, technical, and commercial teams for rapid AI use-case rollout. • Maintain executive-ready reporting for the CEO and COO, including Board materials, management accounts summaries, performance dashboards, and KPI packs. 2. Go-to-Market (GTM) Strategy & Execution GTM Strategy & Commercial Engine Building • Lead strategic initiatives and special projects from the CEO/COO, including major accounts, partnership structuring, and pricing strategy. • Develop and refine GTM strategy across segments (public healthcare, private hospitals, regional markets), aligning commercial pipeline with product and clinical priorities. • Define customer segmentation, ICPs, commercial channels, and expansion roadmaps. Execution & External Engagement • Own execution of GTM plans, including negotiations, contracting, procurement cycles, and stakeholder management. • Partner closely with Sales & Customer Success teams to accelerate pipeline progression, customer onboarding, and product usage. 3. Sales & Customer Success Oversight (As Required) (Especially during VP Sales & CS maternity leave in 1H 2026) • Provide interim leadership of Sales & CS, ensuring continuity of day-to-day sales operations, reporting, pipeline hygiene, and customer engagement. • Mentor junior team members to maintain delivery reliability during the transition period. 4. AI Workflow Integration, Adoption & Scaling This Director will co-lead, with the CEO/COO, the operationalisation of AI use cases across clinical and operational settings. Workflow Integration & Change Management • Engage clinical, nursing, operations, and allied health teams to map current vs future workflows for AI-enabled processes. • Lead workflow redesign efforts to integrate AI tools into patient-care and administrative pathways. • Coordinate closely with project technical leads and PMOs on technology development, integration, and Epic/downstream system alignment. • Ensure implementations meet clinical governance standards and regulatory expectations. Adoption, Implementation & Scaling • Lead institutional rollout of AI use cases: pilots, onboarding, adoption cycles, and scale-up. • Develop implementation playbooks, SOPs, and site-specific operational guides. • Align adoption activities with enterprise-level programmes within health systems, ensuring EndeavourX products land firmly in operational practice. ⸻ 5. Benefits Realisation & KPIs • Support development of benefits cases (throughput gains, staff time saved, clinical efficiency, safety outcomes). • Define and track adoption metrics, usage analytics, benefit realisation, and operational KPIs for AI deployments. • Work with health system PMOs and EndeavourX leadership to feed results into portfolio reporting, quarterly business reviews, and Board updates. • Use metrics to continually refine commercial positioning and customer success narratives. 6. Stakeholder Management • Serve as the connective tissue across clinical, operational, IT, innovation, and leadership stakeholders in NUHS and external clients. • Represent EndeavourX in working groups, customer governance forums, and transformation programmes. • Provide structured updates to PMOs or executive steering committees as needed. • Build trusted senior-level relationships to drive alignment and unblock issues swiftly. Qualifications & Experience • 7–10 years of experience in business operations, GTM, strategy, project management, or healthcare transformation roles in health tech, SaaS, or regulated industries. • Proven experience in startups, scale-ups, or corporate spinouts. • Track record in leading cross-functional initiatives and large-scale operational rollouts. • Excellent communicator with strong senior-stakeholder management instincts. • Experience with healthcare systems, public sector environments, or regulated technology is advantageous. • Familiarity with AI-enabled workflow redesign, digital transformation, or implementation science is a strong plus. Join #TeamTengah #GrowWithUs #TGCH #TGCHFamily Assistant Director, Organisational Development (Tengah General and Community Hospital) The job holder will lead and drive organisation-wide organisational development (OD) strategy and execution for TGCH, with the direction set by the CEO of TGCH to oversee culture(spirit)-building, leadership capability, and organisational effectiveness across all levels. Accountable for shaping and embedding desired values, purpose, and co-design operating models as TGCH transitions from build phase to steady-state operations. Provide strategic direction to leadership, align OD initiatives with institutional priorities, and ensure sustainable impact through measurable outcomes. Job Description: Organisational Development – Strategy & Governance Shape, own, and drive the OD vision, strategy, and roadmap, ensuring alignment with TGCH and cluster-wide strategic and operational priorities, and positioning OD as a core enabler of organisational outcomes. Translate strategy into a phased, adaptive OD roadmap, with clear priorities, sequencing, and interventions across TGCH’s lifecycle (formation, preparation, opening, and beyond). Partner the CEO and senior leadership to shape organisation design, culture, and transformation priorities, ensuring coherence across multiple strategic and operational priorities and agendas. Establish governance, KPIs, and dashboards, enabling regular tracking, leadership visibility, and data-driven decision-making on OD priorities and impact. Organisation-wide Transformation & Execution Lead the design and end-to-end execution of key OD programmes and organisational events, including leadership retreats, alignment workshops, culture-building milestones, and critical pre-/post-opening interventions. Translate OD priorities into structured programmes and engagements, ensuring strong facilitation, clear deliverables, and disciplined follow-through of agreed actions. Drive adoption and embedding of interventions into day-to-day practices, moving beyond one-off events to sustained behavioural and operational change. Ensure organisational readiness at key transition points, proactively identifying risks and deploying targeted interventions to close capability, alignment, or engagement gaps. Leadership & Culture Enablement Enable leadership alignment, team effectiveness, and capability-building through OD interventions and organisational platforms. Partner with L&D and stakeholders to embed leadership and culture outcomes into organisational practices beyond discrete leadership programmes. Stakeholder & System Alignment Work closely with CEO, senior leadership, key stakeholders to co-develop and support OD and organisational initiatives, ensuring alignment with broader organisational priorities. Facilitate alignment through structured engagements (e.g. leadership retreats, planning sessions), supporting shared understanding and direction across stakeholders. Support coordination across institutions, and external partners where relevant, contributing to coherent implementation of OD efforts. Job Requirements: Bachelor's degree required, with Masters or specialised diploma/certification in Organisational Development, Business or HR preferred. At least 14 years of working experience (3 to 5 years in leadership role) with strong track record in organisational transformation, change management, culture building, training and facilitation. Candidates with more extensive and relevant experience may be considered for a more senior position. Ability to work in a fast paced and dynamic work environment, quick thinker and an effective problem solver. Calm, decisive, and resilient in high-pressure situations. Attention to detail, ability to prioritise workload, be well organised and multi-task in a smart and timely fashion. Possess strong analytical, communication, written and presentation skills. Ability to work independently, in a team and across teams with minimal supervision. Possess exceptional interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to develop strong working relationship at various levels. Proactive attitude and determination to ensure required outcomes are achieved and takes responsibility. Strong leadership qualities with the ability to motivate and nurture the team to meet institutional goals. Tech-savvy with an ability to learn new software and other relevant programs. You will gain insight into how the financial services sector in Singapore operates, and the rules and regulations at work. Recognised law degree and admitted to legal practice in Singapore. Preferably with Criminal Prosecution and/or Civil/Commercial Litigation experience. It will be an advantage if you have experience in both prosecution and civil litigation work. Strong writing, analytical and communication skills. Interest in regulatory/enforcement policy formulation. Ability to work well independently as well as in a team. Ability to be nimble and manage multiple deadlines. Applicants should be Singapore citizens You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and needs of stakeholders, as well as the agility to respond to changes and developments. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment. This is a 2-year contract. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 18 Aug 2026. Closing on 13 Sep 2026. Want a front-row seat to how ministry-level strategy is shaped – and a chance to influence it? What the role is: Join MND’s Corporate Strategy team and work with senior leadership to tackle complex, cross-cutting challenges that shape Singapore’s built environment – from housing and land use to urban development, infrastructure, municipal services, technology and resilience. From supporting medium- to long-term strategic planning to navigating emerging risks, you will help translate issues and trade-offs into clear insights for senior decision-making, while building strong foundations in strategy, problem-solving, and stakeholder engagement early in your career. This is a unique opportunity to gain exposure to how strategic issues are framed, discussed and progressed at the senior leadership level, across a wide range of challenges spanning housing, land use, urban development, municipal services, technological change, risk and resilience, while building strong foundations in strategy, stakeholder management, and enterprise risk governance. - Shape strategic priorities and decision-making Support the development and refinement of the MND Family’s medium- to long-term priorities (5–10 years) by structuring issues, synthesising perspectives, and translating strategic considerations into clear papers and discussions. - Drive cross-cutting strategy projects Lead and structure blue sky initiatives that cut across divisions and agencies - bringing together different perspectives to tackle current and emerging system-level challenges, such as public service experience in an AI-driven society. - Shape senior leadership platforms Help design and drive key forums (e.g. senior management retreats and strategic discussions), ensuring that conversations are focused on the most critical issues and lead to clear outcomes. - Strengthen organisational resilience Identify emerging risks and vulnerabilities, and work with stakeholders to develop strategies that enhance the MND Family’s ability to respond to a rapidly changing environment. - Track what matters Develop and refine ways to monitor progress on key priorities, ensuring leadership has a clear, honest view of where things stand - and where course corrections are needed. Why this role - A panoramic view of how Singapore’s built environment is shaped across housing, land use, infrastructure, urban development and municipal services - Exposure to how strategic issues are framed, discussed and progressed at senior leadership platforms across the MND Family - Rare early-career opportunity to experience how large, diverse organisations are managed from the inside - Build a whole-of-system perspective and develop range - Accelerated learning and development in your career - Strong analytical and critical thinking - Clear and structured communication - Ability to engage and influence stakeholders - Ownership and initiative - Interest in strategy, public policy and organisational management Experience: Open to both strong fresh graduates and early-career officers, with relevant internship or strategy experience.

The mission of South Asia, Middle East and Africa Division (SAMEA) is to advance and diversify Singapore’s economic interests in these markets. In the course of our work, we engage a range of partners and stakeholders – government agencies, private companies, business chambers, thinktanks and universities – to grow mutual understanding and build bridges between Singapore and the regions at the government, business and people levels. We seek to open up new market opportunities for Singapore companies, position Singapore as a trusted partner in Asia, and ultimately champion and grow trade and investment between Singapore and the regions. As Deputy Director, you will lead a diverse and dedicated team in engaging our stakeholders in the South Asia, Middle East and Africa Markets. You will support your team to: • Track and analyse key geostrategic and economic developments and trends in your markets and assess their impact on Singapore’s trade and investment interests; • Develop, implement and review strategies, policies and initiatives that enhances Singapore’s bilateral and regional economic relations with countries in SAMEA; • Represent MTI during visits, meetings, negotiations and conferences, and where relevant, lead negotiations and discussions with international counterparts; • Build networks and relationships with foreign stakeholders, including government agencies, private companies, business chambers, thinktanks and universities; and • Drive effective talent management and staff capability development to meet the team’s current and future requirements. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 24 Jul 2026. Closing on 19 Sep 2026. The Family & Early Childhood (FEC) division sits under the Family and Child Development (FCD) Policy Directorate. The FEC division formulates and reviews policies that promote and strengthen families, in support of MSF’s macro outcomes to support marriage and parenthood actualisation and build strong and resilient marriages and families. Families are the bedrock of Singapore society. As Assistant Director (Family Policy), you will shape the policies and strategies that help Singaporeans build strong, resilient families — from supporting marriage and parenthood to ensuring that every child gets a good start in life, and that families are supported to care for elderly members with dignity. You will lead a team of policy officers across three broad areas of work. Strengthening Family Ties and Support Structures You will review and develop policies that promote strong family relationships across all life stages, with a particular focus on ensuring that elderly persons are well-supported by their families as they age. jobs.title: SENIOR EXECUTIVE/ ASSISTANT DIRECTOR (CLIMATE MITIGATION), ECPD
jobs.inst: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 24 Aug 2026. Closing on 07 Sep 2026. At MSE and our family of agencies – PUB, NEA, and SFA – we drive sustainability and resilience initiatives that improve the everyday lives of Singaporeans. As part of the MSE Family, you will be at the forefront of innovation, leading efforts to safeguard water resources, protect public health, and ensure food safety. Through partnerships across sectors, we tackle evolving challenges while fostering an inclusive, safe, and supportive workplace. Join us in shaping Singapore’s sustainable future and making a lasting impact on the everyday lives of generations to come. Climate change poses an asymmetrical challenge for Singapore – we contribute only around 0.1% of global carbon emissions, but will be disproportionately impacted by its effects. In Feb 2021, the Government launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030, a whole-of-nation movement to advance Singapore’s national agenda on sustainable development. In Oct 2022, Singapore announced that it would raise its national climate target to achieve net zero emissions by 2050. There is much work to be done to realise the climate aspirations of Singapore. The available mitigation options have trade-offs, and need to be considered in the context of the overall triple transition of carbon, energy and the economy. Your work will therefore revolve around carefully weighing trade-offs, whether that be in exploring new possibilities for Singapore or ensuring existing policies remain fit-for-purpose. Climate action is a priority for MSE, and is driven by the Energy & Climate Policy Division (ECPD). ECPD is MSE’s coordinating policy desk for issues overseen by the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Climate Change (IMCCC). ECPD drives policies relating to climate science, climate adaptation and climate mitigation, including issues such as carbon pricing, decarbonising Singapore’s economy, coastal protection, and reducing urban heat. You will join the Climate Mitigation team to help Singapore navigate an uneven and complex climate landscape, domestically and internationally. As part of the Climate Mitigation team within ECPD, you will work with a diverse range of stakeholders from the public sector (e.g. NCCS, MTI and various statutory boards), private sector and civil society on a whole-of-nation effort to mitigate climate change. Amongst many other issues, you will be: • Developing strategies to realise carbon abatement through adoption of a variety of low-carbon solutions,from scaling up international carbon markets to promoting energy efficiency nationally; • Reviewing the price of carbon; • Reviewing and strengthening NEA’s capabilities to support low-carbon strategies, e.g. those in relation to NEA’s role as the carbon tax administrator and the national carbon accounting authority; • Developing thought leadership for international climate mitigation issues (e.g. scaling up innovative financing models to facilitate the low-carbon transition) in partnership with IMCCC agencies; and • Supporting inter-agency efforts in driving the triple transition of carbon, energy and economy. We are looking for candidates who: • Can contribute constructively in inter-agency policy reviews, and translate policy intent into implementable frameworks for the statutory boards • Can think critically and handle uncertainty • Have strong analytical skills, and able to see both the bigger picture and fine details • Have strong written and spoken communication skills • Are able to work both independently and within a team, and can actively maintain strong working relationships across agency boundaries.

jobs.jd: Posting Date: 16 Mar 2026. Closing on 18 Sep 2026. Who we are The Legal Policy Group (LPG) in the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) plays a critical role in upholding the rule of law, advancing access to justice, and ensuring a sound and progressive legal framework for Singaporeans. What the role is Under LPG, officers at the Civil & Legislative Policy Division (CLPD) do not just review laws — we play an important role in helping to shape the future of legal policy and governance in Singapore. Our team has driven reforms that touch the lives of Singaporeans every day. Some recent initiatives include: • Relief for victims of harassment: In 2021, we established the Protection from Harassment Court to give victims of harassment faster, more accessible and affordable relief through simplified court processes. • Modernisation of laws: In 2023, we modernised our laws through legislative reforms that make it possible for statutory declarations, oaths, affirmations, and notarisations to be done through electronic means. • Strengthening family therapeutic justice: The Maintenance Enforcement Process (MEP) was introduced in May 2023 under the Family Justice Reform Act to improve the enforcement of maintenance orders, deter non-payment, and improve access to justice for maintenance applicants through efficient enforcement procedures and sustainable outcomes. In 2025, the Maintenance Enforcement Division was established within the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office to administer the MEP, with Maintenance Enforcement Officers working to achieve these objectives. • Enhancing the management of community disputes: In 2024, we worked closely with the MND and MCCY on enhancements to our Community Disputes Management Framework. jobs.title: Legal Associate/Legal Counsel/Assistant Director (Enforcement)
jobs.inst: Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 30 Apr 2026. Closing on 18 Sep 2026. The Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCS) administers and enforces Singapore’s competition, consumer protection and legal metrology laws. Amongst various things, CCS conducts investigations and takes enforcement action in appropriate cases, whilst providing effective advice to the Government and public authorities on national needs and policies in competition, consumer protection and legal metrology matters. (Interested Applicants, please include a cover letter and your education qualification certificates and transcripts in your application) You will assist in the Commission's administration and enforcement of the Competition Act against cartels, dominant companies that abuse their position and mergers which substantially lessen competition. You will also be involved in the administration and enforcement of the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act, the Consumer Protection (Trade Descriptions and Safety Requirements) Act, and the Weights and Measures Act. In this regard, you will play an important role in protecting consumer interests and ensuring fair trading practices, consumer product safety, and a reliable system of weights and measures in Singapore. Your work will include conducting investigations and interviews, participating in dawn raids, gathering field intelligence, assessing notifications (including mergers), working on policy and law reform matters relating to competition law and consumer protection law, and representing the Commission in the Courts and Tribunals, as required. You will also be part of the Commission's team of lawyers, working on policy matters and initiatives, providing legal advice on wide-ranging issues, and assisting to vet and draft contracts. Appointment and remuneration will be based on relevant experience and post-qualification experience (“PQE"). • A recognized law degree, with preferably at least 2-3 years PQE • Called to the Singapore Bar (preferred) • Applicants with no experience but have keen interest in Competition Law and Consumer Protection Law are welcome to apply • A background in Enforcement, Investigation, Prosecution, Litigation, or Economics will be an advantage • Strong communication, teamwork and interpersonal skills • Fresh graduates may apply
